o4.rootCause: Confirmed by experiment: the pre-6ed1a5d0 lint inlined every resource, including each prepared video frame, as a base64 data URL in one page.evaluate payload. Re-applying that inlining to the current lint (prepared media still passed) reproduces the proof's exact O4 error on proof T1 in 9 s: 'page.evaluate: Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation.' The same inlining passes on the 96-frame synthetic fixture (~0.3 MB PNG frames) and on the 60 s 270×480 loop (62 MB), but fails on a 4 s high-entropy 1080×1920 clip derived from the tracked one (571 MB of prepared PNG, close to the proof's 513 MB). The failure scales with payload size, so it is not a Vite reload. 6ed1a5d0 replaced the inlining with a validated-resource middleware (/_lint/assets/<id>) that streams prepared frames from the media cache; the page fetches each frame on demand into its bounded LRU. a5710b8d (same day) moved the renderer import out of page.evaluate into a bootstrap module script.
o4.regressionTests: tests/browser/composition-quality.ts (ET2 section: O4 and O6 fixtures, the no-video control, state-only lint, measured text bounds and decode residency) and tests/browser/composition-media-video-lint.ts (from test:browser:composition-media: a 60 s clip with limits, LRU and cancellation; a proof-scale 571 MB high-entropy clip as the transport regression).

changes.change: Lint's Vite server runs in middleware mode on an owned node:http server bound to 127.0.0.1. A listening Vite dev server installs a process-wide SIGTERM handler that calls process.exit, which skipped the lint's own cleanup. New opt-in options: ownsProcessSignals (launch the pinned browser without Playwright's signal handlers) and collectMediaStatistics (report.mediaStatistics: decode residency plus the decodedFrameBytes budget). Both are absent by default, so existing reports keep their bytes.

launchRenderBrowser({ handleProcessSignals: false }) passes handleSIGINT/handleSIGTERM/handleSIGHUP false to Playwright. Default unchanged; launch flags and RENDER_BROWSER_PROFILE unchanged. Playwright's SIGINT handler always exits with 130 after closing browsers, racing the caller's cleanup (probe: own SIGINT listener present, process still exited 130).

comp lint turns SIGINT/SIGTERM into an AbortSignal for program loading and lint, sets ownsProcessSignals, and reports comp-program-aborted ('Composition lint cancelled by SIGINT|SIGTERM') with exit 1. Listeners are persistent while linting because tsx's signal relay exits when no listener remains. Repeated signals are idempotent: a terminal signals the whole process group and tsx relays again.
Pixel lint paragraph: video/sequence frames come from the prepared export frames within mediaLimits; cancellation behaviour.

measured1080.notes: Peak resident memory was sampled with ps every 250 ms (Node process; descendants are the browser and FFmpeg). The decode LRU peaked at 132,710,400 B (16 frames) against its 134,217,728 B decodedFrameBytes budget. The whole wrapper took 170.6 s with 864 MiB max RSS (/usr/bin/time).

diagnostics.message: Required decoded source exceeds configured allocation limits

default1080.explanation: With default mediaLimits (decodedCacheBytes 8 GiB), preparation rejects the 60 s 1080×1920 clip in 0.04 s, before any decoding. The reservation is raw RGBA per required frame: 1,440 × (1080·1920·4 + 1,920 + 1,024) ≈ 11.95 GB. Actual PNG cache use for the same clip is 493 MB (about 24× less). At defaults, a full-frame 1080×1920 clip fits up to about 1,035 frames (43 s at 24 fps).

cancellation.before: On the base, SIGINT to comp lint (node --import tsx) during media preparation left .media.lock and a .prepare-<uuid> staging directory in the media cache plus a still-shift-compiled-* program directory. During the browser phase it left composition-lint-vite-*. The CLI never connected process signals to the lint's AbortSignal; Node's default action ended the process before any cleanup.
cancellation.afterFirstFix: Wiring signals with process.once still left composition-lint-vite-* on SIGINT (Playwright's handler exits 130 after closing browsers) and on SIGTERM (Vite's listening dev server: close, then process.exit; exit 143 with no report).
cancellation.final: Process-group delivery, like a terminal Ctrl-C. Through node --import tsx and tsx, every SIGINT/SIGTERM in the preparation and browser phases exits 1 with comp-program-aborted and leaves no staging, lock, Vite cache, compiled program or Chromium process. Through pnpm the exit code is pnpm's (130/143), and pnpm can return before its child finishes cleanup; after the child finishes there are no leftovers.
cancellation.library: lintCompositionFile with an AbortSignal: covered by the automated long-clip test (preparation and browser phases).

o8.syntheticClip: No frozen-pixels or frozen-run with the synthetic clip (O4 and O6 fixtures, 60 s loops at 270×480 and 1080×1920). The no-video control reports both over frames 5–83, so the footage's pixels reach the pixel rule.
o8.proofClip: Unchanged from ET0: frozen-pixels over T1 1–15 and 148–167, T2 154–167, T3 1–16 and 144–167 (footage-only spans; mean inter-frame luma ≤ 0.002/255 in 144–167, exactly 0 at 156–157 and 163–167).
o8.policy: Unchanged. Near-static footage counts as frozen in pixel mode (channel delta > 4 on ≥ 200 pixels).

ownerDecisions.question: Should footage that is near-static in encoded pixels (proof frames 144–167) count as motion for pixel stillness?
ownerDecisions.evidence: Pixel lint reports those spans as frozen-pixels because consecutive encoded frames differ by at most 0.002/255 mean luma, with several identical frames. Moving synthetic footage is never reported. State lint no longer reports footage spans (O8 changed in ET0).
options: Keep: near-static footage is frozen; authors add motion or waive the span in policy (current behaviour; consistent with the owner's every-second-moving direction)
Treat any native footage layer as motion regardless of measured pixels
Add an explicit per-layer or per-span stillness waiver for intended footage holds
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Keep the current rule; decide separately whether a footage-hold waiver is wanted.

ownerDecisions.question: Should the default media cache reservation admit a 60 s 1080×1920 clip?
ownerDecisions.evidence: The default decodedCacheBytes (8 GiB) rejects it before decoding, because the reservation is raw RGBA per frame (≈ 11.95 GB). Real cache use is 493 MB. Declaring decodedCacheBytes 16 GiB lints it in 155 s at 1.75 GB peak resident.
options: Keep the conservative reservation; long or high-resolution clips declare mediaLimits.decodedCacheBytes
Reserve from encoded PNG bounds or per decode batch (engine change; affects export too)
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Keep for now and document it; revisit with ET3 or ET8 if real footage hits it.

observations: The default composition media cache (os.tmpdir()/still-shift-composition-media/<sha256 of cwd>) has no eviction. Every distinct prepared source stays until removed by hand. Preparation reserves against the directory's total bytes, so once a checkout's cache passes decodedCacheBytes (8 GiB by default), every new preparation fails with comp-media-limit ('Existing cumulative media cache exceeds configured bytes'). On this machine, after the ET0–ET2 sessions, the per-checkout caches were 4.9 GB (primary checkout), 5.0 GB, 3.5 GB, 3.5 GB and 1.5 GB (this worktree; removed at the end of ET2).
